item.meaning: Mechanical or electrical energy generated by capturing the kinetic movement energy of fast-flowing river currents.
The direct transformation of light energy (solar radiation) into electrical energy using semiconductor solar cells.

item.definition: Power derived from infinite natural phenomena (sunlight, wind, water flow) that generates power without burning fuels or producing atmospheric emissions.
A traditional mountain watermill built over swift streams that uses hydro-kinetic fluid energy to turn heavy stone grinders for milling grain.

item.title: Reaction Thrust Propulsion
item.description: Escaping compressed air stored in an inflated balloon produces an equal and opposite mechanical reaction force (thrust) propelling a attached straw rocket along a string.

item.statement: Energy cannot be created or destroyed in an isolated system; it only changes from one form (e.g., compressed air potential energy) to another (kinetic motion or sound).
Moving fluid streams transfer momentum upon striking curved turbine blades, generating rotational mechanical torque proportional to fluid density, flow rate, and blade area.

item.structure: Curved Spoon Blades on Water Wheels
item.function: Captures maximum fluid momentum from falling stream water, converting linear fluid kinetic force into rotational shaft torque.

groups.properties: Infinite natural supply; produces power with zero smoke, ash, or greenhouse gas emissions.
Finite fossil fuels; releases toxic smoke, soot, and carbon emissions when burned.

item.cause: Releasing compressed air stored inside an inflated balloon taped to a straw rocket.
item.effect: Escaping air produces an equal and opposite mechanical reaction thrust, propelling the straw rocket along a string.

item.setup: Plucking stretched rubber bands of varying thickness stretched across an open hollow cardboard box.
item.observed_phenomenon: Plucking causes rapid visible back-and-forth vibrations of the bands while producing audible sound; thinner stretched bands produce higher pitch.
item.scientific_explanation: Sound is produced by vibrating objects transferring mechanical energy to compress air particles into sound waves.

procedure: 1. Thread a 5-meter string through a plastic drinking straw and tie the string taut between two chairs.
2. Inflate a balloon, pinch the neck closed without tying, and tape the balloon to the straw.
3. Release the balloon neck and observe the straw movement along the string.
item.inference: Compressed air escaping backward produces an equal and opposite forward thrust, demonstrating Newton's Third Law and reaction propulsion.

procedure: 1. Insert plastic spoons radially into the sides of a plastic cup at equal intervals.
2. Push a wooden skewer through the central axis of the cup as a rotational axle.
3. Hold the axle horizontally under a tap or pour stream water onto the spoon blades.
item.inference: Flowing fluid momentum striking curved blades generates rotational mechanical torque, modeling hydro-turbines and gharaats.

item.application_title: Large-Scale Photovoltaic Solar Power (Bhadla Solar Park)
item.practical_use: Harnessing desert solar radiation using large solar panel arrays generates thousands of megawatts of clean electricity, powering lakhs of homes without burning coal or producing smoke.
Utilizing fast mountain stream currents to turn wooden water turbines mills wheat and corn into flour in remote Himalayan villages without electric grid infrastructure.
